title: How to Get a Quote & Pay Your Plumber in Sanur, Bali
meta: How to get a fair written quote, manage prepayment, collect receipts, and confirm warranty terms when hiring a plumber or pool tech in Sanur, Bali.
intro: Getting a leak fixed at your Sanur villa should not feel like a guessing game. Here is how a proper estimate works, what to expect around prepayment, and how to make sure you are not paying twice for the same repair. Keep this short guide handy before you message any local technician.

paragraphs: The simplest way to start is to send photos of the problem on WhatsApp – a dripping tap, a cloudy pool, a cracked tile near the septic tank vent. A good technician will look at the images, ask two or three clarifying questions (age of the pipe, whether PDAM water or well water feeds that line), and give you a ballpark figure for labour plus parts.

For straightforward jobs – replacing a showerhead, clearing a blocked floor drain, topping up chlorine after the rainy season – a photo-based quote is usually enough. For anything involving buried pipes, the rooftop storage tank, or an old villa's original plumbing layout, the technician may need to walk the site first so the number they give you actually holds.
bullets: Send 3-5 clear photos from different angles; include one wide shot showing where the issue sits in the room or yard.
Mention whether the supply is PDAM mains or a bore well – fittings and corrosion differ noticeably.
Ask explicitly: 'Is this price inclusive of materials, or are parts quoted separately?'
If the job touches gas lines or electrical wiring near water, stop and call a licensed professional rather than improvising.

paragraphs: In Sanur most private technicians work on a simple split: a small deposit to cover materials before they leave the shop, then the balance once you have checked the finished work. The exact split depends on the size of the job, so do not expect a fixed percentage rule.

Payment by bank transfer (BCA, Mandiri, BSI) is the norm for expats; cash is fine for smaller jobs but always confirm the total amount out loud before handing over notes. Ask for the account name to match the person who did the work – it sounds basic, but it saves headaches if there is ever a dispute.
You should never feel pressured to pay before seeing the result. If something looks off after the technician leaves, say so within a day or two while the area is still accessible.

sections.h2: Receipts and a Simple Paper Trail
paragraphs: Bali tradesmen are not required to issue tax invoices, but a short written receipt protects both sides. A few lines in your chat history or a printed slip with the date, description of work, parts used, and total paid is more than enough.

Why bother? If your villa's insurance company asks what was done after a burst pipe, or if you are listing the property and want to show maintenance records, that little note becomes genuinely useful. It also makes it easier to hold someone accountable if the same joint leaks again next dry season.
bullets: Ask: 'Can you send me a quick summary of what you fixed and what it cost?' Most technicians will type it into WhatsApp in under a minute.
Save the message in a dedicated folder on your phone – do not rely on memory three months later.

paragraphs: This is where quotes get fuzzy if nobody spells it out. Some technicians include standard fittings (a length of PPR pipe, a washer set) in their labour rate; others buy everything at the hardware shop in Denpasar and add the retail cost plus a small handling margin on top.

In Sanur the sea air accelerates corrosion on exposed metal parts, so ask whether the replacement piece is stainless or brass rather than plain steel. For pool work, confirm that any chemical you are asked to purchase is compatible with what is already in the water – mixing chlorine with other products can produce harmful gas, so stop and call the technician back before pouring anything.

If the job needs a part that is not stocked locally, expect a one- or two-day wait while it ships from Jakarta or Surabaya. Factor that into your schedule, especially during peak rainy season when courier runs slow down.

There is no formal consumer-protection statute that mandates a warranty period for private trades in Bali, which means the 'guarantee' is whatever the technician agrees to with you. Ask directly: 'If this same leak comes back within two weeks, will you come back at no charge?' Get the answer in writing – even a single WhatsApp message works.

A reasonable expectation is that the joint they soldered or the gasket they replaced should hold through normal use for at least a few weeks. If the failure is caused by something outside their control (a tree root cracking the main line, a pressure surge from PDAM switching), that is a different conversation and may carry a new quote.

Keep the original receipt and photos of the finished work. When you contact the technician about a repeat issue, those images make it obvious whether it is the same repair failing or a new problem entirely.

faq.q: Do I have to pay before the technician starts working?
faq.a: Usually only a small deposit to cover materials if parts need to be bought first. The balance is due after you inspect the finished job. Agree on the split before any work begins so there are no surprises.

faq.q: Can I get a fixed price without an on-site visit?
faq.a: For simple, visible jobs (tap replacement, pool filter cleaning) a photo-based quote over WhatsApp is often sufficient. For buried pipes, septic tank issues, or anything inside old villa walls, an in-person look will give a more accurate number and avoid change orders later.

faq.q: What should I do if the same problem reappears after the repair?
faq.a: Message the same technician within a day or two, attach fresh photos, and reference your original receipt. If they agreed to a short workmanship window, they will typically return at no extra labour cost. If the cause is external – tree roots, PDAM pressure spike – expect a new assessment and possibly a new quote.

cta: Got a drip, a cloudy pool, or a mystery smell near the septic vent? Snap a quick photo and send it over on WhatsApp – I will take a look and let you know what the fix involves before you commit to anything.
